Hurricane Harvey was a powerful and devastating ___E:tropical cyclone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone)___ that made ___E:landfall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall)___ in Texas and Louisiana in August 2017, causing catastrophic flooding and more than 100 deaths.

It is tied with ___E:2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ 's ___E:Hurricane Katrina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina)___ as the ___E:costliest tropical cyclone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_costliest_Atlantic_hurricanes)___ on record, [nb 1] inflicting $125 billion (2017 USD) in damage, primarily from catastrophic rainfall-triggered flooding in ___E:Greater Houston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Houston)___ and ___E:Southeast Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Texas)___ ;   this made the storm the costliest ___E:natural disaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_disaster)___ recorded in Texas at the time.  It was the first major hurricane [nb 2] to make landfall in the United States since ___E:Wilma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Wilma)___ in 2005, ending a record 12-year span in which no hurricanes made landfall at the intensity of a major hurricane throughout the country.
In a four-day period, many areas received more than 40 inches (1,000 mm) of rain as the system slowly meandered over eastern Texas and adjacent waters, causing unprecedented flooding.

With peak accumulations of 60.58 in (1,539 mm) in ___E:Nederland, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederland,_Texas)___ , Harvey was the ___E:wettest tropical cyclone on record in the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_wettest_tropical_cyclones_in_the_United_States)___ .
The resulting floods inundated hundreds of thousands of homes, which displaced more than 30,000 people and prompted more than 17,000 rescues.

The eighth ___E:named storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Named_storm)___ , third hurricane, and first major hurricane of the extremely active ___E:2017 Atlantic hurricane season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ , Harvey developed from a ___E:tropical wave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave)___ to the east of the ___E:Lesser Antilles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Antilles)___ , reaching ___E:tropical storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_storm)___ status on August 17.  The storm crossed through the ___E:Windward Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands)___ on the following day, making landfall on the southern end of ___E:Barbados U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados)___ and a second landfall on ___E:Saint Vincent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_(Antilles))___ .

Upon entering the Caribbean, Harvey began to weaken due to moderate ___E:wind shear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear)___ , and degenerated into a tropical wave north of ___E:Colombia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia)___ , late on August 19.  The remnants were monitored for regeneration as it continued west-northwestward across the Caribbean and the ___E:Yucatán Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula)___ , before redeveloping over the ___E:Bay of Campeche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche)___ on August 23.  Harvey then began to ___E:rapidly intensify U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification)___ on August 24, regaining tropical storm status and becoming a hurricane later that day.

While the storm moved generally northwest, Harvey's intensification phase stalled slightly overnight from August 24–25; however, Harvey soon resumed strengthening and quickly became a ___E:Category 4 hurricane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category_4_hurricane)___ later that day with peak 1-minute sustained winds of 130 mph.  Hours later, Harvey made landfall at ___E:San José Island, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jos%C3%A9_Island_(Texas))___ , at peak intensity, followed by another landfall at ___E:Holiday Beach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiday_Beach,_Texas)___ at Category 3 intensity.
Rapid weakening then ensued, and Harvey had downgraded to a tropical storm as it stalled near the coastline, dropping torrential and unprecedented amounts of rainfall over Texas.

On August 28, the storm emerged back over the Gulf of Mexico, strengthening slightly before making a fifth and final landfall in ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ on August 29.  As Harvey drifted inland, it quickly weakened again as it became an ___E:extratropical cyclone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extratropical_cyclone)___ on September 1, before dissipating two days later.

In addition to the huge cost and extent of the damage it caused, Harvey caused at least 107 confirmed deaths: 1 in ___E:Guyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyana)___ and 106 in the United States.
Due to the extensive damage, the name Harvey was retired in April 2018 and will not be used for another Atlantic tropical cyclone.

A westward-moving ___E:tropical wave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_wave)___ emerged from Africa over the eastern Atlantic Ocean on August 12. A surface circulation slowly developed and ___E:convection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_convection)___ consolidated around the low over the subsequent days; the system became a ___E:tropical depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_depression)___ on August 17.  Maintaining its brisk westward motion, the system strengthened slightly and became a tropical storm later that day, at which time it was ___E:assigned the name U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_naming)___ Harvey .

With ___E:maximum sustained winds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_sustained_wind)___ of 45 mph (70 km/h), Harvey made ___E:landfalls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landfall)___ in Barbados and ___E:St. Vincent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines)___ on August 18 before entering the Caribbean.

Hostile environmental conditions, namely ___E:wind shear U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_shear)___ , imparted weakening and caused Harvey to degenerate into a tropical wave by August 19.  Though it lacked an organized surface low, the remnants of Harvey continued to produce significant convection as it traversed the Caribbean Sea and ___E:Yucatán Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yucat%C3%A1n_Peninsula)___ .

The system reached the ___E:Bay of Campeche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Campeche)___ in the ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ on August 23 and soon consolidated around a new surface low.

Late on August 23, the remnants of Harvey regenerated into a tropical cyclone and re-attained tropical storm intensity by 18:00 UTC.  Initial reorganization was slow; however, within a highly favorable environment, the system soon underwent ___E:rapid intensification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_intensification)___ as an ___E:eye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_(cyclone))___ developed and its ___E:central pressure U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_pressure)___ quickly fell. After becoming a hurricane on August 24, Harvey continued to quickly strengthen over the next day, ultimately reaching peak intensity as a Category 4 hurricane.

Around 03:00 UTC on August 26, the hurricane made landfall at peak intensity on ___E:San Jose Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Island,_Texas)___ , just east of ___E:Rockport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockport,_Texas)___ , with winds of 130 mph (210 km/h) and an ___E:atmospheric pressure U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atmospheric_pressure)___ of 937 ___E:mbar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_(unit))___ (27.7 ___E:inHg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inch_of_mercury)___ ).
It made a second landfall on the Texas mainland, at Rockport, three hours later in a slightly weakened state.

Harvey became the first major hurricane to make landfall in the United States since ___E:Wilma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Wilma)___ in ___E:2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Atlantic_hurricane_season)___ .

Once Harvey moved inland, it began to weaken rapidly as its speed slowed dramatically to a crawl, and Harvey weakened to a tropical storm on August 26. For about two days the storm stalled just inland, dropping very heavy rainfall and causing catastrophic flash flooding.

Harvey's center drifted back towards the southeast, ultimately re-emerging into the ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ on August 28. Once offshore, the poorly organized system struggled against strong wind shear.

Deep convection persisted north of the cyclone's center near the ___E:Houston metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_metropolitan_area)___ along a ___E:stationary front U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stationary_front)___ , resulting in several days of record-breaking rain. Early on August 30, the former hurricane made its fifth and final landfall just west of ___E:Cameron, Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron,_Louisiana)___ , with winds of 45 mph (70 km/h).

Associated convection with Harvey became focused north of the center and along a warm front on September 1 as it moved further inland, indicating that the system transitioned into a post-tropical cyclone by 06:00 UTC that day. The remnants continued northeastwards before being absorbed into another extratropical system on September 3.

___E:Tropical cyclone warnings and watches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_warnings_and_watches)___ for the ___E:Windward Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windward_Islands)___ were issued starting at 15:00 UTC on August 17, about six hours before Harvey developed.

At that time, a tropical storm watch was posted for ___E:Dominica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominica)___ , while a tropical storm warning became in effect in ___E:Barbados U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados)___ , ___E:Martinique U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martinique)___ , ___E:Saint Lucia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia)___ , and ___E:Saint Vincent and the Grenadines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines)___ .
All watches and warnings were discontinued by late on August 18, as the storm continued westward into the Caribbean.

In Honduras, a green alert was issued for the ___E:Atlántida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A1ntida_Department)___ , ___E:Islas de la Bahía U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_Islands_Department)___ , ___E:Colón U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Col%C3%B3n_Department_(Honduras))___ , ___E:Cortés U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cort%C3%A9s_Department)___ , ___E:Gracias a Dios U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracias_a_Dios_Department)___ , ___E:Olancho U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olancho_Department)___ , and ___E:Yoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoro_Department)___ ___E:departments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departments_of_Honduras)___ .

About 8 inches (200 mm) of precipitation was expected along the coast, while inland areas were forecast to receive 2.76 to 3.15 in (70 to 80 mm) of rain.  As the remnants of Harvey approached Mexico, the Civil Protection Secretary of the state of ___E:Campeche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campeche)___ issued a blue alert, indicating minimal danger.

When Harvey redeveloped at 15:00 UTC on August 23, the Government of Mexico issued a tropical storm watch in ___E:Tamaulipas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamaulipas)___ from ___E:Boca de Catan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boca_de_Catan)___ to the mouth of the ___E:Rio Grande U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande)___ .
The watch remained in effect until 21:00 UTC on August 25, after it became evident that the storm no longer posed a significant threat to that area.

FEMA worked with the ___E:Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ , ___E:Customs and Border Protection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Customs_and_Border_Protection)___ , and ___E:Immigration and Customs Enforcement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Immigration_and_Customs_Enforcement)___ to prepare for the storm and its aftermath.

The agency placed disaster response teams on standby at emergency posts in ___E:Austin, Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin,_Texas)___ , and ___E:Baton Rouge, Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baton_Rouge,_Louisiana)___ .

Upon the NHC resuming advisories for Harvey at 15:00 UTC on August 23, a hurricane watch was issued in Texas from ___E:Port Mansfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Mansfield,_Texas)___ to ___E:San Luis Pass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Luis_Pass_(Galveston_Island))___ , while a tropical storm watch was posted from Port Mansfield south to the mouth of the ___E:Rio Grande U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Grande)___ and from San Luis Pass to ___E:High Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Island,_Texas)___ .
Additionally, a storm surge watch became in effect from Port Mansfield to High Island.

Additional watches and warnings were posted in these areas at 09:00 UTC on August 24, with a hurricane warning from Port Mansfield to ___E:Matagorda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matagorda,_Texas)___ ; a tropical storm warning from Matagorda to High Island; a hurricane watch and tropical storm warning from Port Mansfield to the Rio Grande; a storm surge warning from Port Mansfield to San Luis Pass; and a storm surge watch from Port Mansfield to the Rio Grande.

As the hurricane neared landfall on August 24, an ___E:extreme wind warning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_wind_warning)___ —indicating an immediate threat of 115–145 mph (185–235 km/h) winds—was issued for areas expected to be impacted by the eyewall; this included parts of ___E:Aransas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aransas_County,_Texas)___ , ___E:Calhoun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calhoun_County,_Texas)___ , ___E:Nueces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nueces_County,_Texas)___ , ___E:Refugio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugio_County,_Texas)___ , and ___E:San Patricio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Patricio_County,_Texas)___ counties.

The watches and warnings were adjusted accordingly after Harvey moved inland and began weakening, with the warning discontinued at 15:00 UTC on August 26. By 09:00 UTC on the following day, only a tropical storm warning and a storm surge warning remained in effect from ___E:Port O'Connor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_O%27Connor,_Texas)___ to ___E:Sargent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sargent,_Texas)___ .

However, watches and warnings were re-issued as Harvey began to re-emerge into the Gulf of Mexico, and beginning at 15:00 UTC on August 28, a tropical storm warning was in effect for the entire Gulf Coast of Texas from High Island northward.

Governor ___E:Greg Abbott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greg_Abbott)___ declared a ___E:state of emergency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency)___ for 30 ___E:counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_counties_in_Texas)___ on August 23, while mandatory evacuations were issued for Calhoun, ___E:Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_County,_Texas)___ , Refugio, San Patricio, and ___E:Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_County,_Texas)___ counties, as well as parts of ___E:Brazoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazoria_County,_Texas)___ , and ___E:Matagorda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matagorda_County,_Texas)___ counties.
On August 26, Governor Abbott added an additional 20 counties to the state of emergency declaration.

Furthermore, the ___E:International Charter on Space and Major Disasters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Charter_on_Space_and_Major_Disasters)___ was activated by the ___E:USGS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USGS)___ on behalf of the ___E:Governor's Texas Emergency Management Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Governor%27s_Texas_Emergency_Management_Council&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , including the ___E:Texas Division of Emergency Management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Division_of_Emergency_Management)___ , thus providing for humanitarian satellite coverage.

In ___E:Louisiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana)___ , Governor ___E:John Bel Edwards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bel_Edwards)___ declared a state of emergency for the entire state.

A mandatory evacuation was ordered in ___E:Cameron Parish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Parish,_Louisiana)___ for the cities of Big Lake, ___E:Cameron U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron,_Louisiana)___ , ___E:Creole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creole,_Louisiana)___ , ___E:Grand Chenier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Chenier,_Louisiana)___ , ___E:Hackberry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackberry,_Louisiana)___ , ___E:Holly Beach U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Beach,_Louisiana)___ , and ___E:Johnson Bayou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_Bayou,_Louisiana)___ .

Additionally, a voluntary evacuation was ordered in ___E:Vermilion Parish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermilion_Parish,_Louisiana)___ for low-lying areas south of ___E:State Highway 14 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Highway_14)___ .

The ___E:Louisiana National Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_National_Guard)___ prepared about 500,000 sandbags and emergency boats and high-water-rescue vehicles were placed on standby should flooding occur.

In ___E:New Orleans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans)___ , there were concerns about whether or not the city's drainage system could handle a heavy rainfall event, with only 105 of the 120 water pumps being operational and some power turbines being out of service.

The city's public schools, as well as six universities and a medical school, closed on August 29.  As Harvey began re-emerging into the Gulf of Mexico on August 28, the tropical storm warning in Texas from Mesquite Bay to High Island was extended eastward into Louisiana to the community of Cameron at 12:00 UTC, while a tropical storm watch was issued from Cameron to ___E:Intracoastal City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intracoastal_City,_Louisiana)___ .

Winds left residents throughout ___E:Barbados U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbados)___ without electricity, with a majority of outages occurring in ___E:Christ Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_Church,_Barbados)___ , ___E:Saint Joseph U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph,_Barbados)___ , ___E:Saint Lucy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucy,_Barbados)___ , and ___E:Saint Michael U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Michael,_Barbados)___ provinces.
Flooding washed one house off its foundation, while water entered some houses, forcing some people to evacuate.
Bridges in ___E:Saint Andrew U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Andrew,_Barbados)___ and Saint Joseph were damaged.
Additionally, a fuel depot in ___E:Speightstown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speightstown)___ was flooded.
Winds from Harvey ripped the roof off a church.
In ___E:Saint Vincent and the Grenadines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines)___ , nine homes were flooded and four others experienced wind damage.
Also, a tree fell on a school, damaging the building.
Blocked drains in ___E:Port Elizabeth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Elizabeth,_Saint_Vincent_and_the_Grenadines)___ resulted in more than 15 businesses being flooded.
A total of 15 people were housed in shelters after the storm.
Strong winds and heavy rainfall also affected ___E:Suriname U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suriname)___ and ___E:Guyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guyana)___ .

In the former, high winds in the capital city of ___E:Paramaribo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramaribo)___ caused roof damage to the ___E:Presidential Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Palace_of_Suriname)___ and two homes, while the Torarica Hotel and Casino suffered structural impact.

Additionally, four dwellings were deroofed in ___E:Commewijne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commewijne_District)___ and three others lost their roofs in ___E:Wanica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wanica_District)___ ; in the latter, the Ministry of Social Affairs building was damaged by falling trees.
In Guyana, the village of Jawalla bore the brunt of the storm.
Four homes were demolished, while five other residences and two shops were damaged.
Several public buildings were also damaged, including the community center, the village council buildings, the nursery, and public schools.
A 29-year-old woman died after her house collapsed on her.
The widespread and catastrophic effects of Hurricane Harvey resulted in one of the costliest natural disasters in United States history.
An estimated 300,000 structures and 500,000 vehicles were damaged or destroyed in Texas alone.
The storm also spawned 53 tornadoes across six states.

The ___E:National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration)___ estimated total damage at $125 billion, with a 90% confidence interval of $90–160 billion.

The scope of flooding in areas with low ___E:National Flood Insurance Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Flood_Insurance_Program)___ (NFIP) participation lends to the large uncertainty in the damage total.

This ranks Harvey as the costliest tropical cyclone on record in the country alongside ___E:Hurricane Katrina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Katrina)___ in 2005. However, accounting for inflation and cost increases since 2005, the National Hurricane Center considers Harvey the second-costliest.

Harvey was the costliest natural disaster recorded in Texas at the time,  until it was surpassed in February 2021 by ___E:a severe winter storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13%E2%80%9317,_2021_North_American_winter_storm)___ that ___E:crippled the state's power grid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Texas_power_crisis)___ , which was estimated to have cost at least $195 billion (2021 USD) in damages in Texas.
Nationwide, 107 people died in storm-related incidents: 103 in Texas, 2 in Arkansas, 1 in Tennessee, and 1 in Kentucky.
Of the deaths in Texas, 68 were from the direct effects of Harvey, the highest such number in the state since 1919.
Twenty-two weak tornadoes touched down throughout the state.
An EF1 tornado near ___E:Fresno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresno,_Texas)___ caused some minor injuries.
Throughout Texas, approximately 336,000 people were left without electricity and tens of thousands required rescue.
Throughout the state, 103 people died in storm-related incidents: 68 from its direct effects, including flooding, and 35 from indirect effects in the hurricane's aftermath.
By August 29, 2017, approximately 13,000 people had been rescued across the state while an estimated 30,000 were displaced.
The ___E:refinery industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Houston#Petrochemicals)___ capacity was reduced, and oil and gas production was affected in the Gulf of Mexico and inland Texas.
On Monday, the closure of oil refineries ahead of Hurricane Harvey created a fuel shortage.
Panicked motorists waited in long lines.
Consequently, gas stations through the state were forced to close due to the rush.  More than 20 percent of refining capacity was affected.

More than 48,700 homes were affected by Harvey throughout the state, including over 1,000 that were completely destroyed and more than 17,000 that sustained major damage; approximately 32,000 sustained minor damage.

Nearly 700 businesses were damaged as well.  Yet the ___E:Texas Department of Public Safety U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Department_of_Public_Safety)___ stated more than 185,000 homes were damaged and 9,000 destroyed.

The hurricane also caused many people to believe that in the wild, only 10 individuals of ___E:Attwater's prairie chicken U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attwater%27s_prairie_chicken)___ remained at most  until Spring 2018, when it was discovered that there were about a dozen wild individuals left.
Heavy rainfall extended eastward into Louisiana, with the state recording up to 14.88 in (378 mm) of precipitation near the town of ___E:Iowa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa,_Louisiana)___ .

In the city of ___E:Lake Charles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Charles,_Louisiana)___ , flood waters reached 4 ft (1.2 m) in height in some areas, with homes inundated and hundreds of people forced to evacuate in one neighborhood alone.
Throughout the state, about 500 people were rescued by August 28, while 269 people went to a shelter in southwest Louisiana, about 200 of whom were rescued from their homes.
An EF2 tornado near ___E:Evangeline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangeline,_Louisiana)___ damaged four homes, one of which was destroyed.
The tornado also damaged fences, a motorcycle, a pickup truck, and toppled three electrical poles.
Rain-slicked roads were blamed for two fatal accidents in ___E:Arkansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas)___ .

In ___E:Alabama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama)___ , an unusually large, long-tracked EF2 tornado in the vicinity of ___E:Reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform,_Alabama)___ and ___E:Palmetto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palmetto,_Alabama)___ damaged two homes and destroyed a barn along ___E:SR 17 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_State_Route_17)___ , while four people were hospitalized for their injuries.

The same tornado also caused damage to trees and roofs in ___E:Lamar County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_County,_Alabama)___ near ___E:Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy,_Alabama)___ and additional damage in ___E:Fayette County U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fayette_County,_Alabama)___ , causing two more injuries.
Another EF2 tornado in ___E:Arab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab,_Alabama)___ destroyed chicken houses and damaged homes and trees.
In ___E:Tennessee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee)___ , more than 19,000 people lost electricity in ___E:Memphis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee)___ .
Low-lying streets in the area were inundated with water.
One indirect death occurred in Memphis due to a weather-related head-on collision of a car and a tractor trailer on ___E:Interstate 40 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_40)___ .
Heavy rainfall in ___E:Nashville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee)___ inundated a number of roads and flooded an apartment complex, resulting in the evacuation of 13 people.
Overall, about 50 people in the city evacuated from flooded areas.
An EF1 tornado also touched down in the northeastern side of the city, damaging trees, homes, carports, and power lines.
An additional EF0 tornado on the southeastern side of the city damaged trees, a carport, a warehouse, and a garage, while also flipping an 18-wheeler.
Rain in Kentucky was blamed for a fatal car accident.
On September 1, the outer bands of Harvey's remnants passed through ___E:North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina)___ .
Severe weather was reported across the central part of the state.
High wind knocked out power in Fuquay-Varina, Sanford, and Holly Springs, and large hail hit parts of Wake, Harnett, and Johnston counties.

In Willow Spring, hail larger than softballs damaged homes and cars. ___E:Flash flooding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flash_flood)___ hit Greenville further east. Tornadoes were also reported in Angier, Clayton, and Smithfield, but they were unconfirmed.

Energy production in the ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ declined in the wake of Harvey by approximately 21% — the output dropped to 378,633 barrels per day from the original 1.75 million ___E:barrels of oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrel_of_oil)___ produced each day. The ___E:Eagle Ford Rock Formation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagle_Ford_Group)___ (shale oil and gas) in southern Texas reduced production by 300,000 to 500,000 bpd , according to the ___E:Texas Railroad Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Railroad_Commission)___ .
Many energy-related ports and terminals closed, delaying about fourteen crude oil tankers.

Houston is located in the ___E:Southeastern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States)___ United States on the ___E:Gulf Coastal Plain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coastal_Plain)___ , and its ___E:clay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay)___ -based soils provide poor drainage.

There is a tendency for storms to move very slowly over the region, allowing them to produce tremendous amounts of rain over an extended period, as occurred during ___E:Tropical Storm Claudette U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Claudette_(1979))___ in 1979, and ___E:Tropical Storm Allison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Allison)___ in 2001.  The area is a very flat flood plain at shallow gradient, slowly draining rainwater through an intricate network of channels and bayous to the sea. The main waterways, the ___E:San Jacinto River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jacinto_River_(Texas))___ and the ___E:Buffalo Bayou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bayou)___ , meander slowly, laden with mud, and have little capacity for carrying storm water.

Houston has seen rapid urban development ( ___E:urban sprawl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_sprawl)___ ), with absorbent prairie and wetlands replaced by hard surfaces which rapidly shed storm water, overwhelming the drainage capacity of the rivers and channels.
Between 1992 and 2010, almost 25,000 acres of wetlands were lost, decreasing the detention capacity of the region by four billion gallons.
However, Harvey was estimated to have dropped more than fifteen trillion gallons of water in the area.

The Katy Prairie in western Harris County, which once helped to absorb floodwaters in the region, has been reduced to one quarter of its previous size in the last several decades due to ___E:suburban development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_sprawl)___ , and one analysis discovered that more than 7,000 housing units have been built within the 100-year floodplain in Harris County since 2010.

As Houston has expanded, rainwater infiltration in the region has lessened and ___E:aquifer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquifer)___ extraction increased, causing the depletion of underground aquifers.
When the saturated ground dries, the soil can be compressed and the land surface elevation decreases in a process called ___E:subsidence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidence)___ .
Subsidence can also occur due to sediment settling.

Specifically, regions to the north and west of the Houston metro have seen 0.4 inches (10 mm) to 1 inch (25 mm) of subsidence per year.  While oil extraction can cause subsidence, in the Houston-Galveston area, most oil has been extracted from sandstone that has relatively negligible ability to compress once oil has been removed.
Thus, oil extraction has not resulted in significant subsidence.
Further, the volume of oil extraction in the Houston area is too low to cause significant subsidence.

The ___E:Gulf of Mexico U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico)___ is known for hurricanes in August, so their incidence alone cannot be attributed to ___E:global warming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_warming)___ , but the warming climate does influence certain attributes of storms.
Studies in this regard show that storms tend to intensify more rapidly prior to landfall.

Weather events are due to multiple factors, and so cannot be said to be caused by one precondition, but climate change affects aspects of extreme events, and very likely worsened some of the impacts of Harvey.

In a briefing, the ___E:World Meteorological Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Meteorological_Organization)___ stated that the quantity of rainfall from Harvey had very likely been increased by climate change.
Harvey approached Houston over sea-surface waters which were significantly above average temperatures.

Warm waters provide the main source of energy for hurricanes, and increased ocean heat can result in storms being larger, more intense and longer lasting, in particular bringing greatly increased rainfall.   ___E:Sea level rise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_level_rise)___ added to the resulting problems.
According to officials from the Harris County Flood Control District, Harvey caused the third '500-year' flood in three years.

The ___E:National Climate Assessment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Climate_Assessment)___ states: .mw-parser-output .templatequote{overflow:hidden;margin:1em 0;padding:0 32px}.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{line-height:1.5em;text-align:left;margin-top:0}@media(min-width:500px){.mw-parser-output .templatequotecite{padding-left:1.6em}}
"The recent increases in activity are linked, in part, to higher sea surface temperatures in the region that Atlantic hurricanes form in and move through.
Numerous factors have been shown to influence these local sea surface temperatures, including natural variability, human-induced emissions of heat-trapping gases, and particulate pollution.
Quantifying the relative contributions of natural and human-caused factors is an active focus of research."

Warmer air can hold more water vapor, in accordance with the ___E:Clausius–Clapeyron relation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clausius%E2%80%93Clapeyron_relation)___ , and there has been a global increase of daily rainfall records.

Regional ___E:sea surface temperatures U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_surface_temperature)___ around Houston have risen around 0.5 °C (0.9 °F) in recent decades, which caused a 3–5% increase in moisture in the atmosphere.
This had the effect of allowing Harvey to strengthen more than expected.
The water temperature of the Gulf of Mexico was above average for this time of the year, and likely to be a factor in Harvey's impact.
The slow movement of Harvey over Texas allowed the storm to drop prolonged heavy rains on the state, as has also happened with earlier storms.
Harvey's stalled position was due to weak prevailing winds linked to a greatly expanded subtropical high pressure system over much of the US at the time, which had pushed the jet stream to the north.
Research and model simulations have indicated an association between this pattern and human-caused climate change.
